publicationFormatMigrationConstraints.status: Read-only design constraints; no production migration implemented or authorized by this diagnostic
publicationFormatMigrationConstraints.formatChange: Existing v1 deflate format supports 8192-byte blocks, but changing fs_format alone would reinterpret every existing block offset and corrupt the filesystem.

requirements.must: Build a separately named block relation using bounded, replayable conversion steps. Preserve all logical file bytes, sparse holes, file lengths, inode identities, modes and mtimes. Verify conversion before atomically activating the new block relation and its matching fs_format metadata. A crash must always expose one complete format, never mixed indices.
requirements.evidence: The offline comparison verified 8,864,202,847 logical bytes and node metadata with identical SHA256 before and after conversion. This proves byte conversion, not a hosted migration protocol.

requirements.must: Existing physical snapshot manifests encode block size and their preimages use the old block indices. The minimal implementation must wait for all active snapshot pins and incomplete imports to finish and be reclaimed through their owners before format activation. Do not forcibly release a live capture or reader merely to migrate. Supporting concurrent old-format snapshots instead requires retaining an explicit old-format block generation and its export/GC protocol. Preserve release tombstones and reader ownership records.
requirements.evidence: Both diagnostic clones deliberately released their own pins; no original pins were changed. They therefore do not validate migration with active captures.

requirements.must: Drain the source serializer, stop admitting new PostgreSQL transactions, finish committed filesystem sync, and close the existing PGlite instance before activating changed block geometry. Reopen with a new DataDirectory/SqliteFS instance after activation; the existing instance caches its format, file handles and decoded blocks. Retain PostgreSQL WAL and other files exactly so normal recovery remains possible. Do not mix a running old-format writer with a new-format block relation.

A full offline conversion held under the source serializer is not a responsiveness solution. If conversion runs while source CRUD continues, it needs an immutable starting image plus complete tracking/replay of changed blocks, new/truncated/unlinked files and inode reuse, followed by a bounded final writer fence. Without that mechanism, require an explicit maintenance window rather than claiming a brief cut. Per-step durable cursor updates and writes must commit together and tolerate lost acknowledgments.

Keep the same Durable Object identity and data_directory generation/complete markers: this is a physical encoding change, not a source reset. Preserve all business tables, computation identities, receipts, sealed output stages, reader-owner ledgers, KV contents, alarms and authentication configuration. Use an existing authorized infrastructure path; do not introduce an unauthenticated migration or arbitrary-SQL endpoint. Do not read, replace or regenerate JWT secrets.

Budget simultaneous old and new block relations, SQLite indices/free pages, PostgreSQL WAL, staging and any retained preimages against the hosted object limit. Track storage during every bounded step and stop before quota exhaustion. The offline probe used native SQLite VACUUM; its compaction behavior and availability through hosted SqlStorage have not been established, so do not assume the same temporary or final size in a production migration.
requirements.evidence: Offline image grew from 2.52GB at 128KiB blocks to 4.65GB at 8KiB blocks. Cloudflare documents a 10GB limit per paid SQLite-backed Durable Object; sql.databaseSize reports its current SQLite size.

requirements.must: Deploy a reader compatible with both persisted geometries before migration. Explicitly handle callers that currently request 131072-byte blocks, since SqliteFS rejects a requested format that differs from storage. Confirm rollback builds can read the promoted format or document that code downgrade is fenced. Test crash/replay before, during and after activation; cold reopen; all active-capture restrictions; byte equality; source CRUD; and preserved authentication and computation receipts. A full-database restore must not silently erase intervening source writes or KV state.

publicationFormatMigrationConstraints.publicationConclusion: 8KiB blocks materially improve the measured write path, but the 8192-row profile still took 12.84 local process CPU seconds. No full 1.38-million-row atomic publication, hosted capacity, or source-serving latency acceptance follows from this diagnostic. Chunking statements inside the same PostgreSQL transaction would still hold the source serializer.
